extracted.intended_audience: CIA leadership, agency procurement/logistics staff, and OFPP/federal procurement policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Assessment and comment on proposed revisions to OMB Circular A-76 governing how federal agencies inventory, review, and (potentially) disclose commercial and industrial activities and contracts, with particular attention to classified/intelligence-sensitive activities. Focuses on procedural requirements (inventories, schedules, disclosure) and conflicts with statutory protection of intelligence sources and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compile complete inventory of all commercial and industrial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately compile a complete inventory of all commercial and industrial activities (those that provide a product or service that could be obtained from the private sector), complete with a description of each activity, the Government's capital investment, annual cost of operation, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate action required under the proposed A-76; the inventory must be detailed enough to show the nature of each activity, government investments, and operating costs. CIA notes that much of this information is classified and that full disclosure would impede protection of intelligence sources and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and furnish a detailed review schedule for each activity and large contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately prepare and furnish a detailed schedule for the review of each commercial or industrial activity and each contract in excess of $100,000 to determine if continued operation is consistent with A-76 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are intended to determine whether activities should remain government-run or be converted to private-sector performance. The requirement includes an explicit $100,000 contract threshold; agencies must produce schedules and make them available to OFPP. CIA expresses concern that security constraints limit its ability to comply with scheduling/disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make inventory and review information available to OFPP and the private sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Make all or substantially all of the inventory and review information available to OFPP and the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed A-76 contemplates sharing detailed activity/contract data outside the agency. The CIA document argues this requirement is infeasible for classified activities because full disclosure to the private sector would expose intelligence sources and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify activities that are 'commercial and industrial' (obtainable from private sector)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and identify which activities are 'commercial and industrial' — i.e., those that provide a product or service that could be obtained from the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definitional step determines scope of inventory and reviews. Agencies must assess each activity's potential for private-sector provision as the first step in A-76 processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with A-76 intent versus literal written requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the agency can comply with the intent of the Circular while recognizing that strict compliance with the written letter may be impossible due to mission-unique constraints (e.g., statutory responsibility to protect intelligence sources and methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CIA recommends advising OFPP that, because of unique mission/security concerns, the Agency 'complies with the intent of the Circular' but cannot comply with certain written requirements without jeopardizing classified operations. This establishes a potential exception/limitation to literal compliance for intelligence agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to OFPP's implementation timeline and comment deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide timely comments and responses to OFPP on proposed changes within the deadlines set by OFPP (example given: requested comments by 23 October 1978).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFPP's 'activist posture' implies aggressive implementation schedules; agencies are expected to meet submission deadlines and coordinate internally (Logistics, General Counsel, etc.) before responding. The CIA document records coordination and recommends formal submission to OFPP.
